candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes a mixed-density (heterogeneous, calcified/ossified) expansile lesion of the maxillary sinus in a 9-year-old boy, consistent with a fibro-osseous lesion such as juvenile ossifying fibroma. Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma is a vascular tumor, would appear hypervascular on imaging, and arises from the nasopharynx rather than the maxillary sinus. Although both can cause facial swelling and orbital displacement in young males, the imaging characteristics (mixed density, bony-hard consistency, well-circumscribed expansile mass) and biopsy approach under local anesthesia (rather than avoidance due to hemorrhage risk typical of angiofibroma) support a fibro-osseous rather than vascular diagnosis. The candidate asserts an incompatible histologic subtype and primary anatomic origin.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma is a vascular fibrous tumor of adolescent males arising from the nasopharynx, not a fibro-osseous lesion; it conflicts with the reference diagnosis of juvenile ossifying fibroma on both histologic subtype and anatomic origin
